findings.body: `factCoordinates()` indexes every requested dimension on both fact types, although `BudgetFact` has no `cost_center`, `section`, `consideration`, `short_name`, `contra_account`, `origin`, or `location`. Consequently Budget facts are grouped under an undefined/missing coordinate and can place the entire Budget in that bucket; because Budget facts are loaded even for Actual-only selections, they can also create a spurious zero-Actual row. This violates the required prohibition on Cost Center Budget allocation and the requirement to support every source-dimension combination exactly. The database test only inspects one cost-center row, so it does not catch the extra/allocation behavior.
findings.title: Not done: Exact answers still allocate Budget to Actual-only dimensions

findings.body: The `no_gl_line` classification unnecessarily requires at least one matching Actual fact. For a scalar selection filtered to a known GL that has no Budget line, querying a completely covered month with no Actual activity makes both fact arrays empty and returns an available Budget of `0.00`, rather than “No Budget line for this GL.” A genuine zero Budget remains distinguishable because its zero-valued line is still present in `budgetFacts`. The analogous Actual-presence guard also causes the Roll-over state to be mislabeled.
findings.title: Not done: Empty-period GL queries lose the required missing-Budget label

findings.body: The new denial, scope, and revocation cases mutate `FakeRbac`, whose `resolveUser()` simply returns an in-memory `AuthUser`. They never exercise the required exported `RbacService.resolveUser` path, so incompatible action/domain/measure/dimension/scope resolution in the real first-party RBAC service would leave this proof green. The test contract permits fakes only at third-party boundaries; QUERY still needs a real-service authorization proof for its refusals and exact resolved scopes.
findings.title: Not done: QUERY proves refusals and scopes only against a fake RBAC resolver

findings.body: Actual values still receive identifiers derived only from a random result UUID; no matching transactions, full count/total, source pin, or permitted scope are prepared or retained. Thus the clickable Actuals cannot yet be opened or paged. Per the stage assignment, the later DRILL/PAGES task must create prepared handles before these identifiers are exposed to consumers.
findings.title: Later: DRILL/PAGES must replace synthetic drilldown IDs with prepared handles

findings.body: The newly committed `QUERY.json` records transient branch/review status and is outside the permitted path set. It is not needed by the query implementation or its tests and should be removed from the change.
findings.title: Simpler: remove branch-local task state → keep only the permitted implementation paths
